headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Aider’s repo writes can expose Khoj-indexed notes and propagate unverified outputs into shared workspaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and can execute shell commands, while Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and serves conversational retrieval. If Aider edits or surfaces prompt-like content in shared files, Khoj may ingest it as context. The pathway is plausible in default shared-repo workflows, though not proven by docs alone.
conditions: IF Aider and Khoj share a repository or indexed folder, injected instructions in files can cross from Aider to Khoj.
IF Khoj indexes Aider-authored files without provenance filtering, file content can be treated as trusted context.
mitigations: Separate Aider-managed repos from Khoj-indexed note folders.
Add a manual review step before Khoj indexes new or edited files.
Use a provenance tag or prefix for machine-authored notes.
Restrict Aider to a dedicated branch or workspace.
requires-engineering: add content provenance filtering in Khoj retrieval.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider has broad network egress and reads/writes repository files; Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and can call cloud or configured search providers. If the same workspace contains sensitive notes or secrets, Aider can access them and its model-provider traffic may exfiltrate context. This is a default-dangerous pairwise leakage path.
conditions: IF sensitive notes or secrets are present in the shared workspace, Aider can read them.
IF Aider or Khoj sends retrieved content to external model/search APIs, those contents can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep secrets and personal notes out of any shared repo or index.
Disable external search/providers for Khoj when handling sensitive notes.
Use separate OS users or containers for Aider and Khoj.
Limit Aider to a narrow repo subtree.
requires-engineering: enforce per-folder access controls and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the filesystem and modify git state; Khoj cannot write files or modify git, but it does maintain a shared index across clients. The main conflict is on shared mutable resources: Aider can change repo files while Khoj reindexes or serves stale content. This is a real overlap, but not the high-severity same-dir write/write case.
conditions: IF Khoj indexes files that Aider is concurrently editing, stale or inconsistent retrieval can occur.
IF both are pointed at the same git-backed workspace, Aider’s commits can race with Khoj’s index updates.
mitigations: Pause Khoj reindexing during Aider edit sessions.
Use a read-only mirror for Khoj indexing.
Keep Aider edits on a separate branch until reviewed.
Schedule index refreshes after commits land.
requires-engineering: add locking or change-detection between editor and indexer.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces code and git commits, while Khoj is a retrieval/chat system that can surface indexed content back to the user. If Khoj treats Aider-authored files or summaries as authoritative, errors can cascade from generated text into downstream decisions or edits. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles.
conditions: IF Khoj presents Aider-generated notes or code snippets as trusted facts, downstream actions may inherit mistakes.
IF the user copies Khoj output back into Aider without verification, errors can loop across both agents.
mitigations: Require human review of Aider outputs before Khoj indexes them.
Mark machine-generated files clearly in the repo.
Use Khoj only for retrieval, not as an authority on code correctness.
Add a checklist to verify citations and code diffs.
requires-engineering: add confidence/provenance metadata to retrieved snippets.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history, while Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents. If personal notes include regulated data and are indexed alongside code, retention and residency obligations can diverge between the two systems. The profiles do not show a specific certification mismatch, so this is a moderate compliance-risk assessment rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in Khoj’s indexed documents and also copied into Aider-managed repos, retention policies may diverge.
IF either system forwards content to external APIs, residency or DPA requirements may be implicated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared repos and indexes.
Document separate retention rules for code and personal notes.
Disable cloud-backed features for regulated datasets.
Review where each agent stores logs and history.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention and residency controls.
